messages.author: ef1bec828cf9a73d
messages.subject: Density Surface Model - R error
parts:
Hi all, 

I am at the stage of modelling the estimated segment-specific abundance as a function of covariates using the DSM engine in Distance.  I am getting an error message from R (in the Distance log files) saying: 

Error in dsm(ddf.obj = ddf.1, formula = Nhat ~ s(Habitat) + s(Dist_water),  : object 'ddf.1' not found

As I understand it, the object "ddf.1" is the result of the detection function modelling that I have done previously in Distance, and the number "1" relates to the analysis number in Distance of the DF that I would like to use (which you select in the drop-down menu in the Model Definition Properties box).  I have tried to run the analyses in the example Dolphin project, and the same error is occurring. 

When I look at the log files for the detection function analysis, there is a warning message:

Warning message: In rm(ddf.dat.1, ddf.1, ddf.summary.1, ddf.table.1) : object 'ddf.table.1' not found

This looks like there is something funny going on with R storing the results of the DF analysis.  I have never tried DSM in R, and this is my first attempt in Distance, so any advice on what the problem is (and how to fix it) would be appreciated.

Matt

messages.author: 350dad0a615d36db
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Density Surface Model - R error
parts:
Hi Matt,

Have you tried re-running the ddf analysis that you wish to use with
dsm? We had some problems with ddf objects from older versions that were
not compatible. This was resolved by simple re-running the ddf analysis.

If that doesn't work, if you can run your analysis in debug mode and
send me a zip file of that folder, I can take a look and see what's
going on. (I will delete your data once I have looked at the bug, of
course.)

best,
--dave

messages.author: ef1bec828cf9a73d
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Density Surface Model - R error
parts:
Hi Dave, 

Thanks for your reply. Fortunately I got some advice from Eric and the problem was that Distance was apparently trying to 'clean up after itself', and so by going into Tools | Preferences | Analysis and un-checking the boxes under "Image Properties", I was able to run the analysis with no problem.

Thanks again, 

Matt
